entries.title: JSON Schema 2020-12 vocabulary system
entries.body: Draft 2020-12 replaces the single meta-schema with a vocabulary system: Core, Applicator, Validation, Annotation, Format, Content, and Unevaluated vocabularies, declared via $vocabulary. A custom dialect can extend or restrict the standard keyword set.

entries.title: $dynamicRef and $dynamicAnchor replace $recursiveRef
entries.body: 2020-12 replaces $recursiveRef/$recursiveAnchor with $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor, enabling extensible recursive schemas where a consuming schema can override a $dynamicAnchor extension point at runtime rather than at authoring time.

entries.title: items / prefixItems restructure for tuples
entries.body: In 2020-12, items is a single schema for additional items; prefixItems is the array of positional schemas (the old positional items). The old additionalItems keyword is gone; use items:false for a closed tuple.

entries.title: unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems see across branches
entries.body: Unlike additionalProperties, unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems are aware of properties/items evaluated by sibling allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if-then-else branches, enabling strict closed-object schemas in composition without losing inherited properties.

entries.title: $ref static referencing and $id base
entries.body: $ref resolves a statically identified schema; $id sets the base URI for resolving relative references. $ref may carry sibling keywords in 2020-12 (OpenAPI 3.0 forbade siblings). Remote refs must be registered (addSchema/loadSchema).

entries.title: if / then / else conditional schemas
entries.body: The if subschema is evaluated; if it validates, then applies, otherwise else applies. Useful for dependent requirements (e.g. require 'card' only when 'type'=='credit') without nested allOf/oneOf chains.

entries.title: allOf / anyOf / oneOf composition semantics
entries.body: allOf requires every subschema pass; anyOf requires at least one; oneOf requires exactly one. With multiple non-null types in `type`, strict validators (Ajv) may require allowUnionTypes to avoid warnings.

entries.title: format is an annotation, not an assertion by default
entries.body: The format keyword is annotation-only by default per the JSON Schema spec. Validators like Ajv require opt-in (validateFormats / ajv-formats) to actually assert formats such as email, date-time, and uri.

entries.title: type can be an array of types
entries.body: type accepts an array of type names, e.g. ["string","null"], to express nullable values. This is the JSON Schema-native approach; OpenAPI 3.1 dropped the proprietary nullable:true in favor of this.

entries.title: const vs enum single value
entries.body: const restricts a value to exactly one; enum restricts to a fixed set. A single-element enum is equivalent to const. enum matches by deep equality and is order-independent.

entries.title: required is an array of property names
entries.body: required lists property names that must be present. In strict mode some validators warn if required properties are not declared in properties. Related: dependentRequired and dependentSchemas.

entries.title: pattern uses ECMA-262 regular expressions
entries.body: pattern validates a string against an ECMA-262 regex. patternProperties maps regex to subschemas for object keys. Beware catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) and unicode flag behavior on adversarial input.
